cues: Its open tiers keep book spines visible, making a room’s reading collection easy to browse.
Narrow horizontal boards span upright supports, creating levels for arranging novels and reference works.
A tall wooden frame can stand against a study wall, with ledges spaced for different volumes.
Adjustable pegs let each level shift upward to accommodate oversized art books or dictionaries.
Dust gathers along exposed ledges where rows of paperbacks sit within easy reach.
A broad lower tier may hold atlases while slimmer upper levels display pocket-sized novels.
The open-backed design lets painted walls show through between neatly aligned rows of books.
Its narrow footprint uses vertical space, keeping a library organized without hiding the book titles.
